findings.description: The user_data script exports AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY as plaintext environment variables. EC2 user data is retrievable from the instance metadata service (and visible in Terraform state/console), so any compromise of the instance or SSRF against 169.254.169.254 leaks long-lived AWS credentials.

No metadata_options block is defined, so IMDSv1 remains enabled. Combined with the credentials embedded in user data and a publicly reachable web server, an SSRF flaw would allow retrieval of the user data and any role credentials without token authentication.
No root_block_device with encrypted = true is specified, so the instance's root EBS volume is created without encryption at rest.

The instance is launched into a public subnet with map_public_ip_on_launch enabled and a route to an internet gateway, giving it a public address directly reachable from the internet alongside a security group permitting SSH from anywhere.
Ingress rule allows TCP port 22 from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing SSH administrative access to the entire internet and enabling brute-force and exploitation attempts against the public instance.
Egress allows all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0, enabling unrestricted data exfiltration and C2 traffic; ingress also permits cleartext HTTP (port 80) from the internet with no HTTPS alternative.
The EBS volume is created without encrypted = true (the attribute is explicitly commented out), leaving data attached to the web host stored unencrypted.
The snapshot is taken from an unencrypted volume, so the resulting snapshot data is stored unencrypted and can be shared or restored without any key control.
The VPC flow log destination bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration, so network flow records containing internal topology data are stored unencrypted.

findings.issue_category: no public access block or bucket policy
findings.description: The bucket defines no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, no ACL restriction, and no policy enforcing aws:SecureTransport, leaving log data at risk of accidental public exposure and permitting cleartext HTTP access.
force_destroy = true with no versioning allows audit/flow log evidence to be deleted or overwritten without recovery, undermining log integrity.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true causes every instance launched in this subnet to receive a public IP, removing the network boundary between workloads and the internet by default.
